# Project rules: electrical shop inventory SaaS

These rules are shared by Claude Code, Codex and Gemini.
Edit only this file and the files in `roles/`, then run `node sync-rules.mjs`.
Never edit CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or GEMINI.md by hand: they are generated.

## Product

- Multi-tenant inventory and billing SaaS for Indian shops.
- First customer type: electrical and electronics shops (the "electrical preset").
- One generic inventory core; shop-type behaviour comes from module switches, never from code that checks the shop type.
- Owner and final decision-maker: Prashant. Only Prashant merges, deploys and holds secrets.

## Stack

- Frontend: Angular 21, standalone components, Signals, new control flow, PrimeNG with our own theme. Do not add Angular Material or Bootstrap.
- Backend: NestJS (TypeScript).
- Database: PostgreSQL with row-level security on every tenant table.
- Jobs and cache: Redis with BullMQ.
- Repository: pnpm monorepo with `apps/web`, `apps/api`, `packages/shared`.
- Hosting: managed services in an Indian (Mumbai) region.
- Open choices (ORM, auth provider, payment gateway, host) are listed in DECISIONS.md. Do not pick one silently.

## Data rules

- Money is integer paise. Quantities are NUMERIC(14,3). Never use floating point for either.
- Never update a stock quantity directly. Insert a `stock_movements` row and update the cached `on_hand` in the same transaction.
- Every tenant table has `tenant_id`. Every query is scoped to the current tenant. RLS policies on all tenant tables.
- Issued bills are immutable. Cancel with a reason or issue a credit note.
- Freeze price, MRP and tax rate on each document line at the time of sale.
- Store timestamps in UTC, show them in IST. Show dates as DD/MM/YYYY. Format amounts with ₹ and lakh/crore grouping through the shared helper only.
- All UI text goes through translation files (en, hi). No hard-coded labels.
- Module switches: `batch_tracking`, `serial_tracking`, `decimal_qty`, `price_lists`, `quotations`, `credit_ledger`, `expiry_tracking`, `pharmacy_compliance`.

## Electrical shop rules

- Wire is stored in metres (base unit). A coil is a batch row with its remaining metres.
- A sale draws from the open coil first, then the next. A coil never goes below zero.
- Serial-tracked items have one `serials` row per unit, with status `in_stock`, `sold`, `returned` or `in_service`. A serial can be sold only from `in_stock`.
- Warranty end = invoice date + the item's warranty months, computed once and stored on the serial row.
- Prices come from the customer's price list, falling back to the item's list price.
- Each role has a maximum discount. A discount above it needs a manager PIN. Warn when price is below cost.
- Quotations move no stock and use their own number series.
- A product has variants (brand, rating, finish). Stock, price and serials belong to the variant.
- Two stores per shop by default: godown and counter. Every movement belongs to a store.

## Indian compliance

- GST type per shop: regular -> tax invoice; composition -> bill of supply with the required declaration line; unregistered -> cash memo.
- HSN code on every item. The required length depends on the shop's turnover band.
- Same state: CGST + SGST. Other state: IGST. Store the customer's state on B2B bills.
- One invoice number series per financial year (April to March). Quotations have a separate series.
- Warn (or block, per shop setting) when a selling price is above MRP.
- DPDP: collect minimal personal data; per-shop export and delete; audit log of sensitive actions.
- Tax and legal facts must come from official sources (GST portal, CBIC, government text). Mark anything unverified as unverified. A CA confirms invoice formats before real shops use them.

## Security

- No secrets in code, commits, logs or prompts. Use environment variables, validated at start-up.
- Never connect to production, run destructive database commands, or change hosting settings. Prashant does those.
- Validate all input at the API boundary. Parameterized queries only. Rate-limit auth and public endpoints.
- The frontend never decides access; the API checks permissions on every route.

## Design

- PrimeNG components only, themed through our design tokens.
- The billing screen is keyboard-first and works with a USB barcode scanner.
- Every screen works on a 1366x768 laptop and a 360 px wide mid-range Android phone.
- Every list screen has loading, empty and error states, pagination and search.
- Follow docs/DESIGN_REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md for every new screen.

## How the three AIs work together

1. Only one AI writes code on a branch at a time. One branch per feature: `feature/<name>`.
2. Every change goes through a pull request. Only Prashant merges.
3. Plan before code for anything bigger than a small fix, and wait for approval.
4. Add tests with every change to stock, tax, serials, billing or tenancy.
5. Reviews are written findings (file, line, severity, suggested fix). Reviewers do not edit files unless Prashant asks.
6. Decisions go in DECISIONS.md. Do not reopen a recorded decision without new evidence.
7. When a rule is unclear, ask. When you finish, list what you did not verify.

## Review limits (to avoid endless reviews)

- Level 0 (text, styling, small fixes): no AI review. Prashant glances and merges.
- Level 1 (normal features): one Codex review.
- Level 2 (stock, coils, serials, billing, tax, tenancy, auth, security): one Codex review, and all tests must pass.
- Gemini audits only at phase gates: end of Phase 2, Phase 3 and Phase 5.
- At most two rounds per pull request: one review, one fix. A second round only for a high-severity finding still open. Then Prashant decides.
- Only high and medium findings block a merge. Low findings go to BACKLOG.md and are fixed in batches.
- Formatting and style are settled by the formatter and linter, not by reviewers. Every finding names a file, a line and a concrete failing case or risk.
- Tie-break order: this rules file, then the tests, then the simpler option, then Prashant's call. The result goes in DECISIONS.md and stays closed.
- AIs do not debate each other. Prashant passes on only the findings he accepts.
- Reviewers: report at most 10 findings, most severe first. Do not repeat a finding already rejected in DECISIONS.md or listed in BACKLOG.md.

## Commands

Use Node 22 (`.nvmrc`). Run from the repository root.

- `pnpm install`: install everything.
- `pnpm dev`: start Postgres (host port 5433) and Redis in Docker, then the API and web dev servers.
- `pnpm test`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm build`: run across all packages.
- `pnpm db:migrate`: run database migrations (added in Phase 1 step 4).
- `pnpm rules:sync`: regenerate CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and GEMINI.md after editing RULES.md or roles/.
